text:
Seth Jones has 23 points in 22 games, 20 of them assists and 15 on the power play, while playing 24.5 minutes a night. That's already most of the 32 points he had in 52 games last season, and his scoring rate of 2.56 points per 60 minutes sits well above our talent range for him (roughly 1.5 to 2.1). Defensemen who run a top power play can stay hot for a while, but this pace leans on the man advantage.

At five-on-five he's solid rather than dominant: Florida takes 54% of the shot attempts and about 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, close to the team's level without him.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking gives the two sides of his game from last season. He stops 18% of the entries aimed at him (typical is 11%), but only 30% of his exits keep possession, so the forecheck is where he can get caught. Evolving-Hockey had him 56th of 215 defensemen, with his biggest value on the penalty kill. Watch how his points hold up if Florida's power play cools.
headline: Seth Jones is running Florida's power play
